# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection via Fake Cracked-Software Site

**Capture window:** 2024-11-26 08:49:38 – 09:43:58 (+0400, timestamps as recorded in pcap)
**Evidence:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap`, `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export)

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (NetBIOS workgroup name `NEMOTODES`; AD domain `nemotoads.health`, DC `NEMOTODES-DC` / 10.11.26.3) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString between 10.11.26.183 and the domain controller 10.11.26.3) |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** Multiple ETPRO/ET signatures fired directly against this traffic:
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` / `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`

This is corroborated behaviorally: every C2 POST carries `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, and the POST bodies exhibit NetSupport's proprietary control protocol (`CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD`, `ES=1`, `DATA=<encoded blob>`) sent to `/fakeurl.htm` on a ~60-second beacon interval, starting at 08:50:45 and continuing through the end of the capture (09:43:29).

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` (plaintext HTTP over port 443, not TLS — flagged by `ET POLICY HTTP traffic on port 443 (POST)`) — primary NetSupport RAT C2, ~60 checkins to `POST /fakeurl.htm`
- `104.26.1.231:80` — `GET /location/loca.asp` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com`, NetSupport client geolocation lookup performed immediately after C2 establishment

**Malicious/suspicious domains:**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` (resolved to 193.42.38.139) — fake cracked-software/APK site, flagged by ET as a "ZPHP" redirect-chain domain in both DNS lookup and TLS SNI; repeated TLS sessions 08:50:14–08:50:40, immediately preceding the NetSupport RAT checkin at 08:50:45
- `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5) and `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207) — visited in the same 08:50:11–08:50:26 window as `modandcrackedapk.com`, consistent with a malvertising/redirect chain leading to the fake-crack page
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231) — legitimate NetSupport infrastructure abused by the RAT for a geolocation check

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — the NetSupport RAT C2 endpoint (repeated POSTs)

**Transferred files / hashes:**
No malware binary was captured in the clear — the actual payload delivery from `modandcrackedapk.com` was over TLS (encrypted), so its file name and hash are not recoverable from this pcap. The only file-like objects observable over cleartext HTTP were the small NetSupport C2 beacon bodies to `fakeurl.htm` (22–260 bytes each, containing `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` protocol data), which are C2 traffic artifacts rather than a dropped file, and legitimate Microsoft/Adobe housekeeping objects (`connecttest.txt`, `ProcessMAU.txt`, `authrootstl.cab`, `disallowedcertstl.cab`) unrelated to the intrusion.

## Summary

At 08:50:11–08:50:40, host DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, user `oboomwald`) browsed through `classicgrand.com` and `confirmsubscription.com` to the fake cracked-software site `modandcrackedapk.com`, consistent with a malvertising-driven fake-crack lure. Within 5 seconds of the last connection to that domain, the host began beaconing to `194.180.191.64:443` using the NetSupport Manager client protocol, confirmed by both Suricata ET/ETPRO signatures and the `NetSupport Manager/1.3` User-Agent and native `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` C2 syntax. Beaconing continued at ~60-second intervals for the remainder of the capture (through 09:43:29), indicating an active, persistent NetSupport RAT infection with attacker C2 access to the workstation. Additional SMB/NTLMSSP and MS-EFSR alerts against the domain controller (10.11.26.3) reflect normal-looking domain-joined workstation traffic and show no separate second-stage compromise in this capture.
